question: Which of the following article of the Indian constitution promotes equal justice and free legal aid?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 39 A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 39A was inserted into the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 and forms part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).

• It directs the State to promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid to ensure that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen because of economic or other disabilities (समान न्याय और नि:शुल्क विधिक सहायता).

• This article is the constitutional basis for the enactment of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, under which NALSA (National Legal Services Authority) was constituted.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• DPSPs are contained in Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) of the Constitution and are non-justiciable in nature.

• The concept of DPSP was borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

• The 42nd Amendment is also known as the 'Mini Constitution'.

NOTE

• Article 38 (Option 2): Directs the State to secure a social order for the promotion of welfare of the people and to minimise inequalities in income and status.

• Article 45 (Option 3): Provides for early childhood care and education for children below the age of six years.

• Article 42 (Option 4): Directs the State to make provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.

question: Who among the following was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karpoori Thakur (Posthumous).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Karpoori Thakur, the former Chief Minister of Bihar known as 'Jan Nayak' (जन नायक), was conferred the Bharat Ratna (posthumously) in 2024.

• He was a champion of social justice and backward-class welfare (सामाजिक न्याय), and the award was announced on the eve of his birth centenary.

• The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, instituted in 1954.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In 2024, a total of five personalities received the Bharat Ratna: Karpoori Thakur, L.K. Advani, Chaudhary Charan Singh, P.V. Narasimha Rao and M.S. Swaminathan.

• The award is not restricted by rank, gender or profession and can be conferred posthumously.

• The medallion is designed in the shape of a peepal leaf.

NOTE

• Lata Mangeshkar (Posthumous) (Option 1): The legendary playback singer received the Bharat Ratna in 2001, not 2024.

• Atal Bihar Vajpayee (Posthumous) (Option 2): The former Prime Minister was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2015 (while alive), not posthumously in 2024.

• Sachin Tendulkar (Option 4): The cricketer received the Bharat Ratna in 2014 and is the youngest recipient; he was not awarded in 2024.

question: In the Union Budget 2025-26, the government has allocated Rs. 20000 crores for an initiative aiming to develop at least _____ indigenously designed and operational SMRs by 2033.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2025-26, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced the Nuclear Energy Mission with an outlay of Rs. 20,000 crore.

• The mission targets the development of at least five (5) indigenously designed and operational Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) by 2033 (लघु मॉड्यूलर रिएक्टर).

• The government has set an ambitious goal of achieving 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047, in line with 'Viksit Bharat'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• SMRs are advanced nuclear reactors with a power capacity of up to 300 MW(e) per unit, offering flexibility and lower upfront costs.

• The mission also proposes amendments to the Atomic Energy Act and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act to enable private-sector participation.

• India's nuclear programme was founded by Dr. Homi J. Bhabha.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 1): Understates the official target; the mission specifically aims for at least five SMRs.

• 10 (Option 3): Not the figure mentioned; the announced number of SMRs by 2033 is five.

• 8 (Option 4): Incorrect; no such figure was cited in the Nuclear Energy Mission announcement.

question: India is ranked _____ in the World Happiness Report published in March 2025.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 118th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the World Happiness Report 2025 (released in March 2025), India was ranked 118th out of 147 countries (विश्व हैप्पीनेस रिपोर्ट).

• The report is published by the Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) in partnership with Gallup and the Oxford Wellbeing Research Centre.

• Finland topped the list for the eighth consecutive year as the happiest country in the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Rankings are based on parameters such as GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perceptions of corruption.

• The theme of the 2025 report focused on caring and sharing.

• Afghanistan was ranked as the least happy country.

NOTE

• 95th (Option 1): Not India's rank in the 2025 report; India stood at 118th.

• 126th (Option 2): This was India's rank in the World Happiness Report 2023 and 2024, not 2025.

• 111th (Option 4): Incorrect figure; it does not correspond to India's 2025 ranking.

question: As per the State of the World's Children 2024, by 2050s more than a third of the world's children will live in four countries. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sudan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per UNICEF's 'The State of the World's Children 2024' report, by the 2050s, more than a third of the world's children will live in just four countries: India, China, Nigeria and Pakistan.

• Hence, Sudan is NOT one of these four countries (सूडान इनमें से एक नहीं है).

• The report examines three major megatrends — demographic shifts, climate crisis and frontier technologies — shaping children's lives.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The State of the World's Children (SOWC) is UNICEF's flagship report, first published in 1980.

• The 2024 edition was titled 'The Future of Childhood in a Changing World'.

• The global child population is projected to remain around 2.3 billion by the 2050s.

NOTE

• China (Option 1): Is one of the four countries projected to host the largest child populations by the 2050s.

• Nigeria (Option 2): Is included among the four countries, driven by high projected population growth in Africa.

• Pakistan (Option 3): Is one of the four listed countries and is therefore not the correct exception.

question: Which of the following became India's first fully solar powered district in May 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2025, Diu (in the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu) became India's first district to meet its entire daytime power demand through solar energy (पहला पूर्णत: सौर ऊर्जा संचालित जिला).

• The achievement was reviewed by Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi.

• Diu set up a solar power plant on rocky, barren land and rooftop solar installations to become energy self-reliant.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The initiative supports India's target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030.

• The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana promotes rooftop solar across the country.

• Earlier, Masali village in Gujarat's Banaskantha became India's first solar-powered border village.

NOTE

• Bhopal (Option 1): The capital of Madhya Pradesh; it has solar projects but is not India's first fully solar-powered district.

• Indore (Option 2): Known as India's cleanest city, not for being the first solar-powered district.

• Nicobar (Option 3): Part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; not the district referred to in this achievement.

question: Ashwini Bhide Deshpande is a renowned vocalist associated with which Gharana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ashwini Bhide Deshpande is an eminent Hindustani classical vocalist associated with the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana (जयपुर-अतरौली घराना).

• The Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana was founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan and is famous for its intricate and complex raga structures.

• A Gharana refers to a system of social organisation in Indian classical music linking musicians by lineage or apprenticeship and a distinct musical style.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Ashwini Bhide Deshpande learnt primarily from her mother Manik Bhide and Ratnakar Pai.

• Kishori Amonkar was another legendary vocalist of the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana.

• She has been honoured with awards such as the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Banaras Gharana (Option 1): A khayal/thumri and tabla tradition; associated with artists like Girija Devi and Pt. Kishan Maharaj, not Ashwini Bhide Deshpande.

• Patiala Gharana (Option 2): Founded by Ustad Fateh Ali Khan and Ali Baksh Khan; associated with Bade Ghulam Ali Khan.

• Kirana Gharana (Option 3): Founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan; associated with singers like Bhimsen Joshi and Gangubai Hangal.

question: Who is the author of the book 'In an Antique Land'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amitav Ghosh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'In an Antique Land' (1992) is a work of history and travel writing authored by the celebrated Indian writer Amitav Ghosh (अमिताव घोष).

• The book blends anthropology, history and memoir, weaving the story of a 12th-century Jewish trader and his Indian slave with the author's experiences in an Egyptian village.

• Amitav Ghosh writes primarily in English and is known for historical fiction.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Amitav Ghosh won the Jnanpith Award (2018), the first English-language writer to do so.

• His famous works include 'The Shadow Lines', 'The Glass Palace', 'The Hungry Tide' and the 'Ibis Trilogy' (Sea of Poppies, River of Smoke, Flood of Fire).

• 'The Shadow Lines' won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1989.

NOTE

• Manu Joseph (Option 2): Author and journalist known for 'Serious Men' and 'The Illicit Happiness of Being Other People'.

• Neel Mukherjee (Option 3): Author of 'The Lives of Others', shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize.

• Siddharth Dhanvant Shanghvi (Option 4): Author of 'The Last Song of Dusk' and 'The Lost Flamingoes of Bombay'.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Love Is Always Right and Other Musings'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinita Dawra Nangia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Love Is Always Right and Other Musings' is authored by Vinita Dawra Nangia (विनीता डावरा नांगिया), a well-known author, columnist and editor.

• The book is a collection of reflective essays/musings on love, life and relationships.

• Vinita Dawra Nangia is also the creator and director of the literary festival 'Write India' and the Times Litfest.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She writes the popular column 'O-Zone' in The Times of India.

• Her other works include 'Just Another Day' and 'The Perfect Woman'.

• She is associated with The Times of India group as a senior editor.

NOTE

• Ravinder Singh (Option 1): Bestselling romance author of 'I Too Had a Love Story' and 'Can Love Happen Twice?'.

• Ravi Subramanian (Option 3): Known for banking-based thrillers such as 'If God Was a Banker' and 'The Bankster'.

• Novoneel Chakraborty (Option 4): Author of thriller-romance novels including the 'Stranger Trilogy' and 'Marry Me, Stranger'.

question: Which of the following folk dance of Chhattisgarh is also known as 'Parrot dance'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Suwa Dance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Suwa Dance is a popular folk dance of Chhattisgarh and is also known as the 'Parrot dance', since the word 'Suwa' means parrot (सुआ अर्थात् तोता).

• It is performed exclusively by women, mainly of the tribal community, who dance in a circle around a pot containing a parrot figure.

• The dance is performed during the festive/marriage season, especially around Diwali.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Chhattisgarh include Panthi, Raut Nacha, Karma, Saila and Pandwani (a narrative form).

• Pandwani was popularised by Teejan Bai.

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in the year 2000.

NOTE

• Kolatam Dance (Option 2): A stick dance of Andhra Pradesh (similar to Dandiya), not related to Chhattisgarh's parrot dance.

• Lambadi Dance (Option 3): Performed by the Banjara/Lambadi tribe, prominent in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

• Aoling Monyu Dance (Option 4): Associated with the Konyak Naga tribe of Nagaland, performed during the Aoleang festival.

question: In the context of space research in India, what does "N" stands for in INCOSPAR?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• INCOSPAR stands for the Indian National Committee for Space Research, where 'N' stands for National (नेशनल/राष्ट्रीय).

• It was established in 1962 by Dr. Vikram Sarabhai under the Department of Atomic Energy.

• INCOSPAR was the predecessor of ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), which was formed in 1969.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• INCOSPAR set up the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.

• Dr. Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the 'Father of the Indian Space Programme'.

• ISRO functions under the Department of Space, and its headquarters is at Bengaluru.

NOTE

• Nano (Option 2): Refers to the nanometre scale (technology); not part of the INCOSPAR acronym.

• Neutrino (Option 3): A subatomic particle; unrelated to the full form of INCOSPAR.

• Nodal (Option 4): Means a central/connecting point; it is not the word represented by 'N' in INCOSPAR.

question: Weight of an object on earth is 441 N. What is the mass of the object?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 45 kg.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Weight (W) = mass (m) × acceleration due to gravity (g), where on Earth g = 9.8 m/s² (गुरुत्वीय त्वरण).

• Given W = 441 N, so mass = W ÷ g = 441 ÷ 9.8 = 45 kg.

• Mass is a scalar quantity measured in kilograms, while weight is a force (vector) measured in Newtons.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mass remains constant everywhere, but weight varies with the value of g at different locations.

• On the Moon, g is about 1/6th that of Earth, so an object's weight becomes one-sixth.

• The SI unit of force/weight is the Newton (N), named after Sir Isaac Newton.

NOTE

• 49 kg (Option 1): Would give a weight of 49 × 9.8 = 480.2 N, not 441 N.

• 41 kg (Option 2): Would give a weight of 41 × 9.8 = 401.8 N, which is incorrect.

• 40 kg (Option 3): Would give a weight of 40 × 9.8 = 392 N, not matching the given value.

question: According to NASA' research, which planet's rings are disappearing at a worst-case-scenario rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saturn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to NASA's research, Saturn's iconic rings are gradually disappearing at a 'worst-case-scenario' rate due to a phenomenon known as 'ring rain' (शनि/Saturn).

• The rings, made mostly of ice and rock, are being pulled into the planet by its gravity and magnetic field as a dusty rain of ice particles.

• At this rate, Saturn's rings could vanish in about 100–300 million years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Saturn is the second-largest planet in the Solar System and is famous for its prominent ring system.

• Data was gathered from the Voyager missions and the Cassini spacecraft.

• Saturn is a gas giant, primarily composed of hydrogen and helium.

NOTE

• Uranus (Option 2): An ice giant with faint, dark rings; not the planet cited by NASA for the fastest-disappearing rings.

• Jupiter (Option 3): The largest planet, with faint dust rings, but not associated with this 'ring rain' finding.

• Neptune (Option 4): Possesses faint rings named after astronomers, but is not the planet in NASA's ring-disappearance research.

question: Around 1713, Sawai Raja Jai Singh of Amer was appointed governor of which region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malwa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Around 1713, Sawai Raja Jai Singh II of Amer was appointed the Mughal governor (Subedar) of Malwa (मालवा) by the Mughal emperor.

• Jai Singh II was a Rajput ruler, astronomer and administrator who founded the city of Jaipur in 1727.

• He served the Mughals under emperors such as Aurangzeb, Bahadur Shah I, Farrukhsiyar and Muhammad Shah.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Jai Singh II built five astronomical observatories called Jantar Mantar at Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, Mathura and Varanasi.

• He was given the title 'Sawai' (meaning one and a quarter) by emperor Aurangzeb.

• The Jantar Mantar of Jaipur is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

NOTE

• Bengal (Option 1): Was a Mughal Subah later ruled by independent Nawabs; Jai Singh was not made its governor.

• Lahore (Option 2): A major Mughal province in the north-west, but not the region he was appointed to govern around 1713.

• Agra (Option 3): Though Jai Singh later held charge of Agra as well, the region specified for this appointment around 1713 is Malwa.

question: Which of the following is correct regarding Sale of government assets like sale of shares in Public sector unit (PSU)?
option_1: It creates liability for the government
option_2: Amount comes from sale of shares are part of capital receipts
option_3: Amount comes from sale of shares are part of revenue receipts
option_4: It does not reduce the total assets of the government
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amount comes from sale of shares are part of capital receipts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sale of government assets, such as disinvestment of shares in a Public Sector Unit (PSU), is classified under Capital Receipts (पूँजीगत प्राप्तियाँ).

• Capital receipts are those which either create a liability (like borrowings) or reduce the assets of the government (like disinvestment).

• Since selling PSU shares reduces the government's assets, the proceeds are treated as capital receipts, not revenue receipts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Revenue receipts do not create a liability or reduce assets — e.g., tax revenue and interest received.

• The nodal body for disinvestment is the DIPAM (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management).

• Disinvestment is the process of the government selling its equity stake in public sector enterprises.

NOTE

• It creates liability for the government (Option 1): Incorrect — sale of shares reduces assets rather than creating a liability.

• Amount comes from sale of shares are part of revenue receipts (Option 3): Wrong — such proceeds are capital receipts, not revenue receipts.

• It does not reduce the total assets of the government (Option 4): Incorrect — selling PSU shares clearly reduces the government's total assets.

question: Following the Industrial Policy _____ of India the government has set up a special board known as Foreign Investment Promotion Board.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1991.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Following the New Industrial Policy of 1991, the government set up the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) to facilitate Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) into India (विदेशी निवेश संवर्धन बोर्ड).

• The 1991 policy marked the era of Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation (LPG reforms), abolishing the 'Licence Raj'.

• The reforms were introduced under PM P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The FIPB was abolished in 2017, and FDI approvals were shifted to the respective administrative ministries.

• The 1991 policy reduced the number of industries reserved for the public sector and removed industrial licensing for most sectors.

• MRTP restrictions on the assets of large companies were also removed.

NOTE

• 1948 (Option 1): The first Industrial Policy Resolution of independent India, which laid down a mixed-economy framework.

• 1956 (Option 2): Known as the 'Economic Constitution of India', it classified industries into three schedules emphasising the public sector.

• 1977 (Option 3): The Industrial Policy that focused on small-scale and cottage industries; it did not create the FIPB.

question: Rani Lakshmibai was defeated and killed in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is June 1858.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi was defeated and killed in June 1858 (17–18 June 1858) while fighting the British at Gwalior during the Revolt of 1857 (रानी लक्ष्मीबाई).

• She fought valiantly against the British under General Hugh Rose, who described her as 'the best and bravest' of the rebel leaders.

• Her real name was Manikarnika (Manu), and she became a symbol of resistance in the First War of Independence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

• The Doctrine of Lapse by Lord Dalhousie — under which Jhansi was annexed — was a key cause of her rebellion.

• Other prominent leaders of 1857 included Tantia Tope, Nana Sahib, Begum Hazrat Mahal and Kunwar Singh.

NOTE

• September 1860 (Option 2): Incorrect date; the revolt was largely crushed by 1858, and she had already died by mid-1858.

• January 1861 (Option 3): Wrong; this is well after her death in June 1858.

• March 1863 (Option 4): Incorrect; by this time the revolt was long over and does not relate to her death.

question: In 2001 – 02, excise duty structure was rationalized to a single rate of _____ per cent CENVAT (Central Value Add Tax).
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2001–02, the excise duty structure in India was rationalized to a single rate of 16 per cent CENVAT (Central Value Added Tax) (केन्द्रीय मूल्य वर्धित कर).

• CENVAT replaced the earlier MODVAT (Modified Value Added Tax) scheme to allow credit of duty paid on inputs and reduce the cascading effect of taxes.

• This simplification was part of tax reforms to move towards a uniform indirect tax structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• MODVAT was introduced in 1986 and later renamed CENVAT in 2000–01.

• Central Excise Duty and CENVAT have now been largely subsumed under the Goods and Services Tax (GST), implemented on 1 July 2017.

• GST is a destination-based, comprehensive indirect tax on the supply of goods and services.

NOTE

• 25 (Option 2): Not the single rationalized CENVAT rate fixed in 2001–02.

• 8 (Option 3): Incorrect; this was not the uniform rate adopted in that year.

• 32 (Option 4): Incorrect and unrealistically high for the single CENVAT rate of 2001–02.

question: The Contingency Fund of an Indian State is held by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Contingency Fund of a State is established under Article 267(2) of the Constitution and is held on behalf of the Governor of the State (राज्यपाल).

• It is an imprest (emergency) fund used to meet unforeseen/urgent expenditure pending authorisation by the State Legislature.

• The Governor can make advances from this fund to meet unexpected expenses, which are later recouped after legislative approval.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Contingency Fund of India (Article 267(1)) is held on behalf of the President of India.

• The three funds of the government are the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account.

• The Consolidated Fund of India is dealt with under Article 266.

NOTE

• Chief Minister (Option 1): The head of the State government/executive, but the Contingency Fund is not held in his name.

• Finance Minister (Option 2): Manages state finances and the budget, but the fund is constitutionally held at the disposal of the Governor.

• State Legislature Speaker (Option 4): Presides over the Legislative Assembly; has no role in holding the Contingency Fund.

question: Which of the following port is confronted with the problem of silt accumulation in the Hugli River?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kolkata port.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kolkata Port (now the Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port) is a riverine port located on the banks of the Hugli (Hooghly) River and is confronted with the persistent problem of silt accumulation (siltation) (गाद जमा होना).

• Continuous dredging is required to keep the navigation channel open for ships.

• It is India's oldest operating major port, commissioned in 1870.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kolkata Port has two dock systems — Kolkata Docks and the Haldia Dock Complex.

• It is the only major riverine port in India.

• Excessive silting reduces the depth of the channel, limiting the size of ships that can dock.

NOTE

• Kochchi port (Option 2): A natural harbour on the Arabian Sea in Kerala; not located on the Hugli River.

• Tuticorin port (Option 3): Now V.O. Chidambaranar Port in Tamil Nadu on the Bay of Bengal coast; not affected by Hugli siltation.

• Chennai port (Option 4): An artificial harbour on the Coromandel Coast; unrelated to the Hugli River's silt problem.

question: What was the primary function of Planning Commission of India?
option_3: To formulate and implement five year plans.
option_4: To monitor the currency exchange system in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is To formulate and implement five year plans.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary function of the Planning Commission of India was to formulate and implement Five Year Plans for the balanced and effective use of the country's resources (पंचवर्षीय योजनाएँ बनाना और लागू करना).

• It was set up in 1950 by a cabinet resolution (not by the Constitution or an Act of Parliament).

• The Prime Minister was its ex-officio Chairman.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The First Five Year Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model and focused on agriculture.

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.

• India's Five Year Plans were inspired by the Soviet (USSR) model of planning.

NOTE

• To control the inflation (Option 1): This is primarily the function of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) through monetary policy.

• To boost the foreign trade (Option 2): Handled by bodies like the Ministry of Commerce and DGFT, not the primary role of the Planning Commission.

• To monitor the currency exchange system in India (Option 4): This function is performed by the RBI, which manages foreign exchange and currency.

question: The National Youth Policy in India launched in February _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2014.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Youth Policy (NYP) was launched in February 2014 by the Government of India (राष्ट्रीय युवा नीति).

• It defines 'youth' as persons in the age group of 15–29 years.

• The policy aims to empower the youth to achieve their full potential and, through them, help India realise its rightful place in the community of nations.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• NYP 2014 identified five objectives and 11 priority areas including education, employment, health and social justice.

• It is implemented by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

• National Youth Day is celebrated on 12 January, the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.

NOTE

• 2001 (Option 1): The earlier National Youth Policy 2003 era; the 2014 policy superseded the previous one, so 2001 is incorrect.

• 2017 (Option 3): Not the launch year of the National Youth Policy.

• 2018 (Option 4): A draft National Youth Policy was later discussed, but the policy referred to here was launched in 2014.

question: Which organ of digestive system secretes the enzyme lipase for digesting emulsified fats in humans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pancreas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pancreas secretes the enzyme pancreatic lipase, which digests emulsified fats into fatty acids and glycerol (अग्न्याशय).

• Fats are first emulsified by bile (produced by the liver) and then broken down by lipase in the small intestine.

• The pancreas is a dual (heterocrine) gland — it has both exocrine (digestive enzymes) and endocrine (insulin, glucagon) functions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Pancreatic juice also contains trypsin (for proteins) and amylase (for carbohydrates).

• The pancreas releases enzymes into the duodenum of the small intestine.

• The endocrine part consists of the Islets of Langerhans.

NOTE

• Gall bladder (Option 1): Only stores and concentrates bile; it does not secrete lipase.

• Liver (Option 2): Produces bile, which emulsifies fats, but does not secrete the fat-digesting enzyme lipase.

• Small intestine (Option 4): The main site of fat digestion and absorption, but the lipase acting here is chiefly secreted by the pancreas.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding haemoglobin in humans?
I. In humans it is the respiratory pigment
II. It has very low affinity for oxygen
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement I is correct: In humans, haemoglobin is the respiratory pigment present in red blood cells (RBCs) that transports oxygen (श्वसन वर्णक).

• Statement II is incorrect: Haemoglobin has a high (strong) affinity for oxygen, not a very low affinity, enabling it to bind oxygen in the lungs.

• Hence, only Statement I is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Haemoglobin is a red-coloured, iron-containing protein; each molecule can carry four oxygen molecules.

• It transports oxygen as oxyhaemoglobin and also carries some carbon dioxide as carbaminohaemoglobin.

• Haemoglobin has an even higher affinity for carbon monoxide (CO), forming carboxyhaemoglobin, which is toxic.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Wrong, because Statement II itself is false — haemoglobin has high, not very low, oxygen affinity.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement II is false.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because Statement I is a true statement about haemoglobin.

question: The summaries of conferences held in ancient India were called _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samhitas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In ancient India, the summaries/collections compiled from conferences or assemblies were referred to as Samhitas (संहिता).

• The word 'Samhita' literally means a 'collection' or 'compilation' of hymns, verses and knowledge put together systematically.

• The Samhitas form the foundational (earliest) layer of Vedic literature.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The four Vedic Samhitas are the Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda Samhitas.

• The layers of Vedic literature are Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads.

• The Upanishads are also called 'Vedanta' (the end/culmination of the Vedas).

NOTE

• Ganas (Option 1): Refer to tribal republics/assemblies (as in Gana-Sanghas) or groups, not summaries of conferences.

• Vedas (Option 2): The broad body of the oldest sacred scriptures; the summarised collections within them are specifically called Samhitas.

• Puranas (Option 3): Post-Vedic texts narrating mythology, genealogies and legends of gods, kings and sages.
